hero_title:
Too many assets?
Let the cat sort them!
hero_lead: NekoNekoAsset syncs the VRChat assets you bought on BOOTH, Gumroad and Jinxxy, downloads, extracts and sorts them, then sends them to Unity in one click. Everything stays on your computer.
mascot_alt: Mascot: a melty white cat sitting in a cardboard box
stores_lead: Sign in to several accounts on each store, and drag in the assets already on your computer too.
booth_desc: Purchases, gifts and free items all sync together.
gumroad_desc: Products in your Library and in Bundles both come along.
jinxxy_desc: Brings your whole Inventory home in one go.
local_desc: Drag in assets you downloaded before. Your original files are never touched.
feat_title: What the cat does for you
feat_lead: Sync, download, sort and send to Unity, all in one place.
sync_desc: Sign in once. Every time you open the app, new purchases appear in your list, so you never page through order history again.
dl_desc: ZIP, RAR and 7z are extracted automatically with their folders intact, and Japanese filenames never turn into garbled text. Original unitypackage files are kept.
find_desc: Clothes, hair and accessories are sorted for you. Add tags, mark which avatars an item fits and build collections. Search works for Japanese titles too.
unity_desc: Tick the files you want. Unity shows its import preview first and writes nothing until you confirm. Needs the free NekoNekoAsset Bridge in your project.
import_desc: Drag in folders and ZIPs to manage them too. The app copies them into your library and leaves the originals untouched.
spend_desc: Totals per currency, counted only from proven payments. Hit certain milestones and the app sets off fireworks.
theme_desc: Sakura, Lemon, Peach, Lilac and more built-in themes, or mix your own colors. The app speaks 5 languages.
shot_note: Real app screens, filled with made-up demo data
shot_alt_sync: Source sync window with BOOTH, Gumroad and Jinxxy accounts syncing
shot_alt_downloads: Files tab: avatar variant packages downloaded and a ZIP being extracted
shot_alt_find: Asset list narrowed down to one compatible avatar
shot_alt_unity: Unity import window with packages from three products selected
shot_alt_import: Import window with a folder, a ZIP, a thumbnail and a tag added
shot_alt_spending: Spending summary with separate JPY and USD totals
shot_alt_themes: Settings with the Sakura dark theme selected
steps_title: Three steps and you are in
step1_desc: It lives on this computer by default, or choose an external drive or a NAS. Assets take a lot of space, so pick a roomy disk.
step2_desc: Sign in on each store’s official login page. The app keeps only the signed-in session and never handles your password. You can also skip this and use it offline.
step3_desc: When sync finishes you can search, download and send to Unity. Auto download is off by default, so you decide what gets downloaded.
privacy_title:
Your data lives
only on your computer.
privacy_lead: NekoNekoAsset has no servers of its own and collects no usage data. Your accounts, purchase history and asset files never pass through the developer.
p_pw_desc: You sign in on the store’s official page. The app keeps only the cookie issued after sign-in, encrypted with Windows DPAPI so only your Windows account can unlock it.
p_cloud_desc: The database, thumbnails and assets all live in the folder you choose. No sign-up, no cloud sync.
p_track_desc: No telemetry, analytics, ads or crash reporters.
p_open_desc: MIT licensed. Every line of code is on GitHub for you to check.
conn_lead: Every connection is listed here. Nothing hidden.
conn_stores_desc: Sign-in, syncing your lists and downloading the files you bought
conn_github_desc: Reading public version info and downloading updates
conn_ai_desc: Only the text and images you select
conn_bridge_desc: Moves files only inside your computer (localhost)
conn_server_desc: They don’t exist, so nothing is ever sent there.
conn_note: If you sign in to a store with Google, Apple or X, the app also connects to that sign-in service while you sign in.
faq_lead: Privacy is usually what people care about most, so we start there.
faq1_q: Does NekoNekoAsset know my store passwords?
faq1_a: No. You sign in on the store’s official login page that the app opens, so your password goes straight to BOOTH, Gumroad or Jinxxy. NekoNekoAsset never reads or stores it. It keeps only the login cookie the store issues after you sign in, and uses it to read your own purchase lists and download your own files.
faq2_q: Where is my sign-in data stored? Could someone take it?
faq2_a:
Each account’s sign-in data is stored separately in your user folder on this computer and encrypted with Windows’ built-in DPAPI. Only the same Windows user on the same computer can decrypt it, so a copy on another computer is useless. Sign-in data never goes into your library, backups or exports.

A note of caution: if your computer already runs malware under your account, no local app can fully protect against it, so keep your system secure.
faq3_q: Are my purchase history and library uploaded to the cloud?
faq3_a:
No. The database (SQLite), thumbnails and downloaded files all stay in the library folder you choose. NekoNekoAsset has no account system and no developer server, and it never uploads or backs up anything to the cloud.

If you put your library inside a cloud-synced folder such as OneDrive or Dropbox, it is that sync software that uploads it, not the app. We recommend a local drive or a NAS.
faq4_q: Can the developer see my data? Is usage data collected?
faq4_a: No, and no. The app has no telemetry, analytics, ads or crash reporters. The only developer-related connection is reading a public version file from GitHub at startup to check for updates, and that request contains none of your accounts, purchases or assets.
faq5_q: Exactly where does the app connect?
faq5_a:
Here is the full list:

  • The stores you sign in to (BOOTH, Gumroad, Jinxxy) and their image and file servers: syncing your lists and downloading files you bought.
  • The service you use to sign in to a store (for example Google, Apple or X): only while you sign in.
  • GitHub: checking for and downloading app updates.
  • The AI service you set up: only when you turn AI on and use it.
  • Product pages whose URL you paste: to fetch public product details when you import local files.

Unity Bridge moves files only inside your computer and never connects to the internet.
faq6_q: Where does the AI feature send my data?
faq6_a:
AI is off by default. To turn it on you enter your own API key. The app then sends only text from the items you select (such as names, tags, filenames and excerpts from included documents) and the images you explicitly choose, to the one AI service you picked. You can also use a local model running on your own computer.

Thumbnail analysis is off by default too, and images are scaled down to 1536px or less first. Login cookies, download links and asset archives are never sent.
faq7_q: Where are AI API keys stored?
faq7_a: In Windows Credential Manager, each key separately. They stay on this computer and never go into your library, backups, exports or logs.
faq8_q: Do backups, exports or “Copy diagnostics” include private data?
faq8_a: Backups and exports never include sign-in data or API keys. “Copy diagnostics” copies only fixed-format status and counts (such as which step a job stopped at and how many retries happened), without accounts, orders, product names, URLs or file paths. It only goes to your clipboard, and you decide whether to share it.
faq9_q: Is it safe to keep my library on a NAS or use it from two computers?
faq9_a:
Yes. A library can be open on only one computer at a time. The app locks it automatically so simultaneous writes cannot damage it; close the app and the other computer can take over.

Sign-in data, API keys and AI chat history stay on each computer, so you sign in to your stores again when you switch computers.
faq10_q: How do I remove my sign-in data?
faq10_a: In account settings, click “Sign out” or “Delete” to clear that account’s session and encrypted cookies on this computer. When deleting an account you can choose to delete its asset records too; downloaded files are kept. AI keys can be removed in AI settings.
faq11_q: Could Unity Bridge mess up my project?
faq11_a: The Bridge only receives files from the app inside your computer, over an authenticated connection, and never connects to the internet. Every import shows a preview in Unity first and writes only after you confirm. If an import fails, it cleans up only the files that import newly wrote and that have not been changed since.
faq12_q: Is this an official tool? Is it risky to use?
faq12_a: It is not official. NekoNekoAsset is an unofficial open-source project made by an individual and is not affiliated with BOOTH (pixiv), Gumroad, Jinxxy, VRChat or Unity. The app reads your own purchase lists with your own sign-in, limits its request rate and waits as long as servers ask. Please check each platform’s terms yourself and make your own call.
faq13_q: Why does the installer show “Windows protected your PC”?
faq13_a: The installer is not signed with a paid code-signing certificate yet, so SmartScreen may warn you. Only download it from this site or the project’s GitHub Releases. Once you have checked the source, click “More info” → “Run anyway”. In-app updates verify their signature before installing.
faq14_a: It is completely free and open source under the MIT license.
faq15_a: Only Windows (64-bit) for now. macOS and Linux are not supported yet.
faq16_q: Will it download all my assets as soon as I sign in?
faq16_a: No. Auto download is off by default, and sync fetches only product details and thumbnails first. You decide what to download, and you can turn on auto download in settings later.
faq17_a: No. You only need the NekoNekoAsset Bridge, installed in a Unity 2022.3 or later project, if you want one-click import into Unity. It comes as a unitypackage, a UPM package and a VPM package.
faq18_q: Why are some items missing from “All”?
faq18_a: BOOTH also sells plenty of things unrelated to VRChat, so the default “All” view shows only VRChat-related assets. Everything else is still saved: you can find it under “Unclassified” or change an item’s category yourself.
